subject: Admin activity chain-of-custody and ad-hoc export runbook
messages:
From: Sally Wu <sally.wu@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit request: admin activity evidence for SOC2 scope

Hi Vanessa —

As we prepare for our SOC 2 Type 2 fieldwork (Q1 testing start), the auditor has asked for a clear statement of what admin activity Redwood logs, how long those records are retained, and the standard ways we can export them (ad‑hoc export + regular snapshots). They also want a short chain‑of‑custody note describing who has access to the export and how we ensure tamper evidence for delivered bundles.

Can you send a short runbook or checklist for:
- admin activity categories (login, role changes, API key lifecycle, console actions, config changes)
- retention defaults and any per-customer configurable retention windows
- export formats (CSV/NDJSON/signed snapshot), delivery options (S3, secure Drive link), and recommended verification (hashing/signature)
- any available automation (scheduled snapshots to customer S3, what RBAC is applied)

We need this by EOD Thursday (11/05) to share with our auditor. If there's an example export bundle or playbook, please attach.

Thanks,
Sally
Sally Wu
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Wu <sally.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit request: admin activity evidence for SOC2 scope

Sally —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a short runbook and an example ad‑hoc export. High‑level summary below; attaching a short playbook and CLI steps. Laura and Karthik are looped for the retention/export details.

Summary (tl;dr):
- What we log: authentication attempts (success/fail), console UI actions (user/role creates/deletes/edits), API key create/revoke/rotate events, model routing/policy changes, instance lifecycle events (start/stop/scale), and admin IAM policy changes. Each event includes timestamp (UTC), actor (internal user/service or external API key), affected resource, action, request_id, and full request payload when applicable.
- Retention: default 13 months for admin action index; 3 years available on request for enterprise contracts (we keep snapshots and signed bundles).
- Export options: ad‑hoc NDJSON or compressed CSV, signed SHA256 manifest; delivery via customer S3 (preferred), secure share link (time‑limited) or our portal bundle download.
- Chain of custody: exports are produced by the audit runbook process (RBAC‑limited runbook role), bundled on an isolated host, signed with a key stored in HSM/KMS, and a SHA256 manifest is generated and logged to an immutable ledger entry. Access to the export artifact is restricted to the customer contacts and Redwood security SME.

Attachments: admin_activity_export_playbook.pdf (playbook), ad_hoc_export_cli_steps.txt (CLI), example_manifest.sha256.txt

We will follow up with a sample export and precise S3 lifecycle guidance by Thursday EOD.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sally Wu <sally.wu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit request: admin activity evidence for SOC2 scope

Adding technical notes and exact commands for the export path (see attached CLI snippet). Key points for the auditor:

1) Event schema: we export NDJSON lines with fields: event_ts (ISO8601 UTC), actor_id (internal_username or API key id), actor_type (user/service), action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, metadata (freeform string). PII in payloads is redacted by default unless the customer requests raw payload export under contract.

2) Retention & snapshots: default retention = 13 months. Customers on Dedicated/Private can configure retention up to 3 years. Snapshot workflow:
   - Run snapshot job (internal job id) which copies nightly compressed bundles to a staging S3 bucket (us-east-1)
   - Run signing step (KMS sign) that produces a manifest.sha256 and a detached signature
   - Promote bundle to customer delivery bucket or generate a time‑limited signed URL

3) Export CLI (example):
   redwood export admin-activity --account acme-health --start 2026-01-01 --end 2026-10-31 --format ndjson --delivery s3://acme-health-audit-bucket/2026Q3/ --sign-with-kms alias/redwood-audit

4) Verification: we recommend auditors verify the SHA256 manifest and the signature (we provide the KMS public cert chain). We also log the export run_id and delivery target to the customer audit ledger for traceability.

I've attached ad_hoc_export_cli_steps.txt that has the exact commands and a short S3 bucket policy snippet.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sally Wu <sally.wu@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit request: admin activity evidence for SOC2 scope

Thanks — this is exactly what we need. We reviewed the playbook and CLI steps; a couple quick clarifying questions for the auditor:
- Can you confirm whether console UI actions include read‑only config fetches or only mutating actions? (Auditor asked about read access to sensitive configs.)
- For the signed bundle, can Redwood include the run_id and the KMS key thumbprint in the manifest?

If you can confirm those two items, we’ll package and send to the auditor. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sally
